featured_reviews.name: Mayur
featured_reviews.review_text:
This restaurant, located near Ghatkopar bus depot on Link Road and close to the Eastern Express Highway.

Since we was traveling around we decided to give a try but it turned to disappointment. Don't fall into the trap of its appearance. At first, the photos, high review count, and name may convince you, but it's a big NO. The hotel management is not malvani. The owner was unavailable, and the staff, who were not Maharashtrian, struggled to understand some things. There was lot of negative reviews about poor service and rude behavior from staff, but we didn't experience any such issues. They were good, albeit lacking some services, like not providing a finger bowl. The place was empty, with no waiting time. Although four AC units were installed, with three of them on, it still felt hot.

Now, about the taste - we ordered multiple dishes (see pictures), but they didn't meet expectations. Except for the 'Banjara kebab' and 'tandoori lollipop', I didn't enjoy much else. The 'bombil fry' was good but overpriced. They should add two more pieces for rate they added. The 'chicken fry' dish was the worst, containing bones instead of being boneless. Avoid it at all costs. The 'manchow soup' was just okay, and the 'prawns fry' wasn't impressive either. The thalis we tried - crab, king surmai, and special chicken - were below average.

The ambiance was more than okay, but the biggest reason to avoid this place is its pricey menu. We've tried many Malvani restaurants, but this one's rates were almost 1.5 times higher, without justifying the taste.

The final verdict is to avoid it if you crave good taste, all my 6 family members were unhappy and lastly, the restaurant should focus on reducing rates.

featured_reviews.review_text:

Visited this place with my friends after hearing a lot about it, and it truly lived up to the expectations. We had a fantastic experience—both the food and the overall vibe were excellent.

We ordered Bombil fry as a starter, along with Prawns Thali and Surmai Thali. Every single dish was 10/10. Personally, whenever I try a new place for fish, I judge it by the taste of the Bombil fry—and this one was outstanding. It was extremely fresh, perfectly crispy, and the masala was well balanced and nicely blended.

The same quality and freshness reflected in the Surmai and Prawns thali—authentic taste and very satisfying portions.

On the owner’s suggestion, we also tried their Mutton Thali for a change, and it was surprisingly excellent. The mutton was fresh, tender, and full of flavour, which is rare to find these days.

If you’re a seafood lover, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy quality fish with great taste and vibes.

featured_reviews.name: Amrita Kamath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Came across this place by chance as it is situated in a bylane not easily visible. The Google reviews made me tempted to try it and I am glad to have visited this place.

The mandeli fry was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft of the inside. The taste of the coating was excellent and the combo with the green chutney and onion was superb 👌 A must try for appetizer!

Malvani prawns gravy was excellent too. It had a balanced spice level, and the prawns size and quantity was sufficient for 2 people. A must try!

The rice bhakri we had with the prawns needs a special mention, as it was super soft and thin unlike those thick and dry bhakris very common in many places.

The prawns pulav too was good in taste, and needs to be tried with a fish gravy to enjoy the combination.

A warm and cozy place, with the ambience trying to match the cuisine they serve, this place is a must try for those looking for home-cooked, freshly prepared Maharashtrian-style seafood cuisine.

While the preparation does take some time, but it is worth the wait, as we know it is being freshly prepared.
Those unwilling to wait can call and order in advance.

Great food, great flavours! We went here for lunch on a Friday afternoon  - it was quite packed - recommend reservation.

We ordered: Bombil fry and Surmai for starters. Followed by Prawns Gassi, Rawas Pulimunchi with Neer dosa and Malabar paratha. I personally liked the curries with the neer dosa better. We finished off with kulfi and caramel custard for dessert.

One of their staff came with a big plate of their different curries - gassi, Malvani, pulimunchi, Goan, etc. He let us taste all of those and explained the flavour profile of each. The neer dosa was raw and felt like one dosa had been cut in half and served as two. The squid was just about bearable, but by then the overall experience had already ruined the meal.

featured_reviews.name: Santosh Mane
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently enjoyed a wonderful family dinner at this gem in Ghatkopar. 🍴 The food was flavorful and thoughtfully prepared based on regional tastes, pleasing both kids and adults alike.

Hospitality stood out throughout making everyone feel welcome 🤝.

Having such a special food stop offering all key maharastrian recipes in Ghatkopar and proximity is a big plus. We loved Tambada/pandhara rassa, Solkadhi, and delicious non-veg khandeshi dishes 😋.

Highly recommend this restaurant in Ghatkopar for a family outing. Great food, excellent service, genuine hospitality, and a convenient location—perfect for creating lasting memories.
We’ll be definitely visiting again!

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Review
“I recently visited this Kolhapuri Malvani restaurant and had a fantastic experience. The food was absolutely delicious, full of authentic flavors and perfectly cooked. Every dish had that rich, traditional taste which truly represents Kolhapuri and Malvani cuisine.
The service was also very good – staff were polite, quick, and attentive. The ambience was clean and comfortable, making it a great place to enjoy a meal with family and friends.
Overall, I really loved the food and would definitely visit again. Highly recommended for anyone who enjoys spicy and authentic Maharashtrian food!”

featured_reviews.review_text: Great value for money, wonderful choice of pan-Maharashtra food - mostly non-vegetarian, but also some good vegetarian options. We were told there's a significant wait time on weekends, but we were lucky to be seated within a few minutes of arriving. Will surely visit again.

featured_reviews.name: ABHISHEK
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Copper Chimney at R City Mall, Ghatkopar, and the experience beautifully reflected their legendary 53-year legacy. Celebrating their 53rd Anniversary, they are offering an amazing 53% off on their iconic Originals Since 1972 and Autograph Dishes, making the visit even more special.

We began with their signature Kadak Roomali with Black Chana Dip, followed by refreshing mocktails like Dalchini Sherbet, Spice Punch, Mumbai Mastani and Anar Kali each one perfectly crafted.

In starters, the original signature Achari Chicken Tikka and Paneer Tikka were smoky, soft, and full of bold flavours. For mains, the Rogan Josh (Lamb) stood out with its deep, aromatic Kashmiri curry notes, and the Palak Goolar Kofta impressed with its creamy almond-cashew gravy and rich spinach–mawa–fig stuffing.

The breads Punjabi Onion & Mirch Roti, Garlic Naan, and Butter Lachcha Paratha paired perfectly with both veg and non-veg curries.

We ended our meal with their signature dessert Muzaffar, thick Lucknowi rabdi topped with roasted vermicelli, and a soft, creamy Rasmalai the perfect sweet finish.

From flavours to service to legacy, Copper Chimney truly lives up to being a classic since 1972. A must-visit for anyone who appreciates authentic North Indian cuisine, timeless recipes, and warm hospitality. Highly recommended!

Ambience & Space

Ambience + helpful staff make it nice for evening outings.

Ideal cost for two is around ₹1,000

feel certain items are overpriced for the portion sizes.
